entries.title: The quiz remembers whether you got it right
entries.body: Each answer the quiz checks is kept with its right-or-wrong judgement, so a right answer stays deeper green after you reload the page. That judgement sets when the question comes back: a day after a wrong answer, a week after a first right one, then twice as long after each further right one, up to 56 days. Answers the check could not judge come back after 3 days, as every answer did before.

entries.title: Quiz colours are explained in the margin
entries.body: Pointing at a quiz question in the margin beside the article explains what its colours mean, and an answer from the day before reads 'a day ago'. Once a question is due to be asked again, your old answer stops shaping the lead-in to the next question and the 'Where to look again' suggestions.

entries.title: Quiz judgements appear in your downloads
entries.body: When you download an article's data, your quiz answers include the right-or-wrong judgement, and the 'Your words' download names it, with a warning that the automatic check can be mistaken. The privacy page says this judgement is kept and what it is used for.
